output.brief:
The rise in cancellations is mostly not a pricing problem. It comes from the Quillbook accounting connector. Quillbook retired its old invoice interface on 30 March. Since then the connector has silently dropped or doubled invoices: 58,300 across 1,212 accounts. Of those accounts, 34% have cancelled, against 8% of Quillbook accounts with no recorded failure. Churn among Quillbook-connected accounts rose to about 6% a month, and the rise is the same for price-locked Founders accounts. Accounts with no connector are flat at about 1.9%, whatever their seat count, so the price rise shows no effect there. The finance seat-band pattern is explained by larger accounts being more likely to use Quillbook. Slow support responses are probably a contributing factor, but that is unproven. The Tallymarsh effect is within normal variation, though its error log hasn't been reviewed.

Next steps: make the Quillbook v3 fix the top engineering priority, and schedule it now (it is currently an unscheduled Sev-3 ticket). Contact every affected account, including those that cancelled, to correct their invoices. Keep the duplicate-invoice hold on. Don't roll back the price, which would cost about $220k a month. Don't start the Tallymarsh rebuild until its log has been reviewed. Confidence is high.
